title: A Robot Snake That Could One Day Travel Through Your Gut
content: MIT researchers have developed a soft, snake-like robot that can move through the small intestine, potentially helping doctors examine hard-to-reach parts of the gut, take biopsies and deliver drugs.

title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
content: AISA leader Neha Bora's refusal to sign peace bonds led to obvious comparisions with the CJP leadership who opted to comply with conditions set for their release from detention during Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests. The CJP faced significant challenges in organizing Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests which was a contrast from their previous successful mobilization. Bora's determination to protest despite multiple detentions brought her to the centre stage of anti-SIR protests.

title: Manisha Bhanwala becomes India's first women's world wrestling champion
content: In a breathtaking gold medal bout, Manisha overturned a daunting 0-6 deficit to defeat Pan American champion Abigail Nette 8-6. Refusing to surrender despite falling behind early, the Indian wrestler mounted a remarkable comeback to turn the contest on its head and secure a historic victory.

title: Dravid, Sehwag named in India squad for U19 Asia Cup
content: Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag have been named in India's squad for the upcoming ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup. The tournament will be held in Muscat, Oman, from November 5 to 14. The 17-year-old Anvay and 19-year-old Aaryavir earned their places after impressive performances in the recently concluded Vinoo Mankad Trophy.

title: Melinda French Gates says her 2-day rule helps employees know they did a good job
content: Melinda French Gates implements a 48-hour feedback rule for employees to manage work conflicts effectively. This approach allows employees to feel secure in their performance evaluations as surprises are avoided. She emphasizes the importance of giving honest feedback with integrity while maintaining respect. Recently, Gates pledged $215 million to improve women's health and called for better accountability in healthcare systems.

title: Two friends turn $15 Denver haunted house into 18 Halloween attractions
content: Two friends, Chris Stafford and Warren Conard, opened a haunted house in a Denver shopping complex in 2002, charging $15 per ticket. What began as a side business has grown into a multimillion-dollar company with 18 seasonal Halloween attractions across the US. The company paid around 4,500 workers during the 2025 Halloween season and is now expanding into Christmas entertainment.

title: Gold hits one-year low, silver slips below $50 as inflation fears bite
content: Gold and silver prices have plummeted to their lowest in a year as energy costs surge and inflation remains a pressing concern. The decline in precious metals mirrors waning investor confidence, driven by fears over persistently high interest rates set by the US Federal Reserve. Furthermore, weak demand from major Asian markets is further stifling gold sales, contributing to the downturn seen in platinum and palladium as well.

title: India's forex kitty shrinks by $1.27 billion as gold reserves slide
content: In the week ending October 23, India witnessed a decline in foreign exchange reserves, dropping by $1.269 billion to a total of $719.748 billion. This decrease was primarily driven by a notable reduction in the value of gold reserves. However, foreign currency assets saw a rise of $1.358 billion, reaching $593.205 billion.

title: Jharkhand women turn Rs 2 savings into Rs 6 lakh ragi collective
content: Kunwari Barwa's initiatives began with a self-help group where women saved small amounts of money together. As the group expanded, they formed a farmer producer organisation focused on ragi cultivation and product sales. The collective now boasts 1,501 members and generates monthly sales of Rs 6 lakh to Rs 7 lakh. Women involved gain employment opportunities and experience market exposure through fairs and exhibitions beyond their village.

title: Meet Landon Hoberman: Teen’s campaign prevents 8.1 million plastic utensils
content: Landon Hoberman, a 17-year-old from New Jersey, has made remarkable strides in reducing plastic cutlery usage in restaurants. His campaign has succeeded in keeping over 8 million utensils out of landfills, while restaurants collectively saved more than $200,000 by making cutlery optional for takeaway. This initiative showcases how small changes can lead to significant environmental impact and financial savings, presenting a scalable model for communities seeking to tackle single-use plastics.

title: Anthropic’s Daniela Amodei questions OpenAI’s Pentagon deal: Was it opportunistic
content: Daniela Amodei from Anthropic has raised concerns regarding OpenAI's recent agreement with the Pentagon and its implications. She suggested that OpenAI may have seized an opportunistic moment while disregarding ethical principles. The disagreement stems from Anthropic's refusal to allow military use of their AI technology, leading to significant tensions with OpenAI. Following this dispute, Anthropic has initiated legal challenges against the Pentagon's actions.

title: Jason Statham’s £20m coastal estate faces scrutiny over summerhouse use
content: Jason Statham and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley are facing challenges in planning the summerhouse at their Hampshire estate. They have submitted a request for a certificate of lawfulness to transform the structure, initially approved as a swimming-pool pavilion, into residential quarters. Although the summerhouse has served as guest accommodation for prior owners since 2012, the New Forest National Park Authority is currently assessing the appropriateness of their application.

title: 'Keep it short': Nia Patel recalls being silenced at grandmother's memorial
content: Nia Patel faced interruption while speaking about women's rights at her grandmother Krishna Ahooja-Patel's memorial. Her grandmother was an influential peace activist and advocate for women's rights, nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize. Nia's experience demonstrates the challenges women still face regarding respect and recognition in discussions about gender issues. The incident illustrates a gap between institutional commitment to gender justice and actual practice.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $325M KC Current opens soccer doors for kids
content: The Kansas City Current launched a free youth soccer league in July to help children overcome financial barriers to sports. The program provides 120 players aged 8 to 10 with uniforms, Nike cleats and equipment at no cost. Supported by community partners, the initiative also offers coach stipends and referee training for teenagers. The league aims to expand access, support local families and encourage greater participation, particularly among girls.

title: Tyreek Hill’s Chiefs reunion in doubt as Kansas City explores WR alternatives
content: The Kansas City Chiefs’ potential reunion with Tyreek Hill is losing momentum as concerns over his knee injury and off-field issues complicate a possible move. Instead, Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs has emerged as an alternative trade target. With Rashee Rice sidelined and the receiving corps struggling, Kansas City must strengthen Patrick Mahomes’ supporting cast before the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

title: U'khand chopper crash: All 6 killed, bodies found; contact lost 2 mins after take off
content: A helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation crashed near Joshimath, resulting in the death of all six people on board. The aircraft lost contact during its flight from Badrinath to Dehradun on Friday afternoon. Search and rescue teams were deployed to locate the crash site amid adverse weather conditions, including heavy rain and snowfall.

title: Jio Q2 results: Profit jumps 14% to Rs 8,389 crore, revenue up 11.4%
content: In its Q2 FY27 report, Jio Platforms recorded a robust net profit increase of 13.7% year-on-year. Operational revenues surged to Rs 40,475 crore, marking an 11.4% rise. The company welcomed 9.1 million new customers, pushing its total to 542.4 million. Furthermore, average revenue per user (ARPU) improved to Rs 218.8, driven by heightened data usage, while voice traffic held steady at 1.52 trillion minutes.

title: Dolly Parton's free-book charity raises over $150,000 after her death
content: In the wake of Dolly Parton's passing, the Imagination Library saw a remarkable increase in registrations. In August alone, Knox County welcomed nearly 950 new children to the program. Additionally, over $150,000 was generated through a fundraising initiative to bolster the library's mission. Established in 1995, this program ensures that young readers receive free books every month until the age of five, proudly distributing over four million books to date.

title: Meet Sophia Parekh, 12, who has given away over 8,000 books in US
content: Sophia Parekh, a 12-year-old from Westfield, New Jersey, has distributed more than 8,000 free books to children across the US through Sophia's Book Stand, a project she started at age seven during the Covid pandemic. She personally selects books based on children's ages and interests and also supports teachers in underserved schools. Her efforts earned her recognition as a runner-up for the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes.

title: Indiana woman wins fight to keep home after ex-partner's brother seeks sale
content: In a legal victory, Gina Behny has maintained ownership of her house after a dispute with her ex-partner's brother, Terry Curella. Purchasing the home in 1999 with help from her grandparents, Behny's extensive investments over 25 years were key. The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's ruling, noting Behny's substantial financial input against Curella's slight involvement, alongside an order for Curella to pay Behny for incurred losses.

title: 6 years, 10 matches, 1 defeat: Team India's unbeaten run comes to an end
content: Team India faced a significant setback as New Zealand achieved an 87-run victory in Auckland. Glenn Phillips and Jacob Duffy played critical roles in New Zealand's decisive performance. India struggled in their chase after losing early wickets and could not sustain their innings. New Zealand posted their highest-ever T20I total of 259 runs, which India could not match.

title: Punjab cop tests positive for drugs during anti-narcotics protest
content: A police officer named Sehajpreet Singh has been arrested for drug consumption during protests in Mansa. Residents found him in an unstable condition at ITI chowk, prompting their protests against him. Police conducted a dope test, confirming his drug use, but no drugs were recovered from him. The incident has led to unrest in Budhlada, with accusations against local officials.

title: Turbulence continues for Saudi flyers as Air India extends flight curbs till Nov 14
content: Air India and Air India Express have announced the extension of flight suspensions to Saudi Arabia until November 14. IndiGo and Akasa Air have also cancelled flights to various cities in Saudi Arabia until mid-November. The flight cancellations are due to heightened security concerns amid unrest in West Asia. Fresh Houthi activity has prompted heightened security measures near Mecca, impacting regional shipping.

title: Quebec home built using plastic from 200,000 bottles, shell assembled in 3 days
content: In a remarkable development, a two-bedroom house located in Saint-Rémi-d'Amherst, Quebec, has been built using an innovative construction method known as PakVert. This technique employs panels crafted from recycled plastic bottles, resulting in a building process that took merely three days. By minimizing construction waste and cutting costs by approximately 35 percent, this initiative contributes significantly to affordable housing and environmental sustainability in Canada.

title: Two Renaissance plaques in family's hallway sell for over £100k after 142 years
content: A pair of exquisite 16th-century maiolica plaques by renowned artist Francesco Xanto Avelli recently fetched an impressive £100,000 at auction after lying unnoticed in a Dorset home for years. The family unearthed these extraordinary pieces while seeking expert advice, discovering they were part of a significant series illustrating the tale of Cyrus the Great. This auction underscores the remarkable rarity and cultural value of these Italian Renaissance treasures.

title: Tennessee wife gets 75% of home equity after judge values house at $160,400
content: In a contentious marital dispute, a Tennessee appeals court confirmed the trial court's assessment of a marital home valued at $160,400, awarding the wife 75% of the home's equity—approximately $47,139. The husband's higher valuation based on comparable sales was dismissed by the court. Moreover, the court invalidated the husband's artwork and tool valuations, mandating their reassessment. It also made essential amendments to the permanent parenting plan concerning visitation rights.

title: Delhi sister demands answers over brother's hit-and-run death, faulty CCTV
content: On the fateful night of October 24, 2026, Prince Singhal, aged 24, became the victim of a potential hit-and-run incident in Delhi, leaving his family grappling with grief and the urgent need for answers. Diya Singhal, his sister, highlights the issue of broken surveillance cameras along the route of the accident, complicating efforts to gather vital evidence.

title: From 3-0 to 87-run defeat! Phillips shatters India's clean sweep dream
content: India had already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series and were looking for another win. However, a record-breaking batting performance from Glenn Phillips and Michael Bracewell helped New Zealand pull off a massive victory. After winning the toss, India decided to bowl first. But the decision proved costly as the hosts smashed 259/7 in 20 overs, their highest-ever total in T20Is. Chasing the mammoth target, India managed only 172/9 in their 20 overs.

title: Arkansas court upholds $3m award for 1.62 acres after 11-year road dispute
content: A long-standing legal dispute in Arkansas involved a land acquisition that significantly impacted property access. The Arkansas Court of Appeals recently upheld a $3 million jury compensation award related to this case. The case emerged after the Arkansas State Highway Commission's project restricted access to a property owned by the William Major Lewis Trust. Evidence submitted demonstrated that the remaining property value was adversely affected by the highway work.

title: Marco Simoncelli’s parents pay emotional tribute 15 years after his death
content: Fifteen years after Marco Simoncelli lost his life in a tragic MotoGP crash at Sepang, his parents, Paolo and Rossella, have shared an emotional tribute to their son. Ahead of the 2026 Malaysian Grand Prix, they posted pictures of the memorial plaque at the crash site with a message.

title: Georgia parents' $37m verdict cut to $2m, appeals court raises it to $3m
content: A couple in Georgia has triumphed in their legal battle, securing a $3 million judgment after an appeals court re-evaluated their son's death case. This decision overturned a previous reduction of a $37 million jury award to just $2 million. Their son, who succumbed to stage-four Burkitt lymphoma, faced complications during his treatment. The court recognized the parents as distinct entities under state law, enabling them to seek higher restitution.

title: Damaged da Vinci-linked painting bought for $1,175 in 2005 sold for $450m
content: In 2005, art dealers acquired Salvator Mundi for just $1,175, initially attributing it to an artist from Leonardo da Vinci's circle. After extensive restoration and research, the painting was presented as a work by Leonardo in 2011. Its value soared dramatically, culminating in a record auction price of $450.3 million in 2017. The painting's current location remains uncertain, with reports suggesting it is stored in a secure vault in Geneva.

title: Why some hugs stay with us for years, according to study of 15,000 adults
content: A newly released study explored the emotional power of hugs and how they shape our memories. By surveying over 15,000 adults, researchers found that feelings of comfort, support, and connection heavily influenced these memories. The analysis revealed interesting gender differences in remembering hugs, highlighting that individuals with high empathy recalled emotionally significant experiences more vividly. Additionally, personal attachment styles played a role in how people viewed their memorable hugging moments.

title: Global LNG prices jump 6%: Is India's gas affordability under pressure
content: The global energy sector is currently undergoing major upheavals that have pushed LNG prices and transport expenses to new heights. Indian oil marketing firms are suffering marked losses on petrol and diesel due to the surge in crude procurement costs. Though there has been a rebound in Middle Eastern crude exports, lingering supply chain challenges remain.

content: Rodrigues injured her hamstring on August 3 while playing for English franchise Southern Brave in The Hundred.

title: California court overturns husband's $39,000 legal fee award filed too late
content: A California man who won a $39,000 legal-fee award against his wife during their divorce proceedings has lost it after an appeals court ruled that he filed his claim too late. The couple had settled their competing restraining order requests in January 2024, but the husband sought legal fees 14 months later. On Wednesday, the appeals court overturned the award.

content: 69 people were killed and more than 200 injured in the deadly train collision . it occurred after a failure in the railway signalling system forced trains to switch to a degraded operating mode . the train was travelling at an estimated 160-200 kmph when it slammed into the stationary train .

title: 'Arrest heads of Arab parties for stealing elections': Israel minister Ben Gvir
